Hi Samir / Olivia — digging into specifics below based on your current VectorHub setup (1024-dim):

1) Vector dimension recommendation
- Redwood's current text embeddings (recommended for semantic search) are 1536 dims for our latest models; we also support 1024/768 variants for lighter workloads.
- For migration: two options
  a) Re-embed corpus to 1536 to get parity with Redwood models (recommended for long-term quality).
  b) Use a projection step if you must keep 1024 for indexing cost reasons (we can provide a linear projection matrix, but re-embedding is preferred to avoid embedding space mismatch).

2) Similarity metric & normalization
- Use cosine similarity; implement L2 normalization on vectors at write-time to allow fast dot-product equivalence (cosine(u,v) == dot(norm(u), norm(v))).
- We recommend normalizing after generation (we can also return L2-normalized vectors directly if you set normalize=true in the embedding API call).

3) Batching guidance
- Inference (online): set dynamic batching up to 128 queries per batch for sub-50ms tail latency on Dedicated pools; larger batches for cheaper throughput if latency SLO is relaxed.
- Re-index (offline): use batch sizes of 512–2048 depending on GPU memory; use concurrency to saturate IO. We'll provide a sample job script.

4) Migration strategy (minimize downtime)
- Hybrid approach: run Redwood embeddings in parallel and keep VectorHub index live. For reads, do a weighted fan-out: query both indices and merge scores (can run A/B or canary on subset).
- After verification, full cut-over: re-index to Redwood's 1536 dims and update routing.
- If re-embedding cost is a blocker, you can project 1024->1536 then re-rank with contextual reranker (we can help tune).

5) SDK / auth / routing notes
- SDK: our JS/Python SDK supports bulk embed endpoints and auto-retry. Example snippet (Python):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
  embeddings = client.embeddings.create(model="embed-text-1536", input=batch_texts, normalize=True)

- Auth: standard Bearer API keys; for Dedicated/Private deployments we support scoped keys and mTLS.
- Routing: include header x-redwood-routing: "region=us-west;pool=dedicated-42" to prefer your Dedicated pool. Fallbacks route to compatible hosted variants.

6) Metrics to validate during pilot
- Recall@10, MRR, average query latency (p50/p95/p99), and embedding drift (cosine distribution).

Attachments: small sample export (embeddings-sample.csv) with VectorHub IDs + text + existing vector (1024 dims) to help plan re-index.
